answer: An agent economy resists Sybil attacks through acoustic multilateration. Nodes authenticate by emitting a synchronized acoustic pattern, like an audio sonnet, recorded across fixed receivers spanning an ocean pier to a cedar grove. An attacker incurs inescapable capital costs provisioning distinct, geographically separated physical loudspeakers per identity. However, localized gusts and thermal gradients distort acoustic transit times, intermittently rejecting legitimate agents.
